source_title: Performance evaluation of an emergency department in Rio de Janeiro: a hybrid approach using Discrete Events Simulation and Data Envelopment Analysis
locator: Methods, Table 2 (timestamp availability); Results, Table 6 (mean service time and 95% CI by shift).
source_setting: Single emergency department in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil; reception, nurse triage and emergency consultation; two shifts (T1 daytime, T2 nighttime).
source_period: Monthly data shown February 2022 through July 2023; service-time sample period is not separately specified.
source_n: Administrative encounter records; stage-specific n not reported. Triage service-duration field was missing in 55.07%; consultation duration missing in 16.46%.
quantity: Observed mean nurse triage service time, T1 and T2
unit: minutes per triage service; 95% confidence intervals
source_evidence_basis: Primary observational hospital-record study reports shift-stratified empirical means and confidence intervals. These are service durations, not queue waits; the paper reports a high missingness rate for the source duration field.
limitations: Single Brazilian hospital and shift-specific results; over half of triage duration values were missing. No empirical distribution family or individual quantiles are reported, and this mean must not be converted into one.
inferred_scenario_use: External reference for a triage service-time mean and uncertainty interval in sensitivity scenarios; do not use as an RWJ measurement or fabricate a service-time distribution.

source_title: Performance evaluation of an emergency department in Rio de Janeiro: a hybrid approach using Discrete Events Simulation and Data Envelopment Analysis
locator: Methods, Table 2 (timestamp availability); Results, Table 6 (mean service time and 95% CI by shift).
source_setting: Single emergency department in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil; emergency physician consultations in two shifts (T1 daytime, T2 nighttime).
source_period: Monthly data shown February 2022 through July 2023; service-time sample period is not separately specified.
source_n: Administrative encounter records; consultation stage n not reported. Consultation duration field missing in 16.46% of records.
quantity: Observed mean emergency consultation service time, T1 and T2
source_evidence_basis: Primary observational hospital-record study reports shift-stratified empirical means and confidence intervals. Service time is distinct from the time patients wait for a consultation.

inferred_scenario_use: External reference for shift-specific consultation service means in scenario sensitivity; retain as means and do not derive a distribution from them.

source_title: Performance evaluation of an emergency department in Rio de Janeiro: a hybrid approach using Discrete Events Simulation and Data Envelopment Analysis
locator: Results, Table 6 (average length of stay at reception by shift); Methods, Table 2 (timestamp availability).
source_setting: Single emergency department in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil; front desk/reception stage, two shifts (T1 daytime, T2 nighttime).
source_period: Monthly data shown February 2022 through July 2023; service-time sample period is not separately specified.
source_n: Administrative encounter records; reception stage n not reported; reception timestamp field missing in 16.86%.
quantity: Observed average length of stay at reception, T1 and T2
source_evidence_basis: Primary hospital-record paper gives empirical shift means and confidence intervals. The table labels the measure reception length of stay; it should not be assumed to be clerk touch time alone.
limitations: Single Brazilian hospital; reception time definition may include non-service time. Stage n is not given, and the reception timestamp field has missing records.
inferred_scenario_use: External proxy for reception-stage elapsed time; keep separate from clerk service time and queue waiting, and do not transfer as RWJ timing.

source_title: Performance evaluation of an emergency department in Rio de Janeiro: a hybrid approach using Discrete Events Simulation and Data Envelopment Analysis
locator: Results, Table 7 (simulation input); Appendix, distribution-fit table (T1 triage input and fit statistics); statistical data analysis section (claimed goodness-of-fit result).
source_setting: Single emergency department in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil; simulation distinguishes daytime T1 and nighttime T2 triage processes.
source_period: Underlying hospital records cover monthly data shown February 2022 through July 2023; exact fitting window not specified.
source_n: Underlying stage sample n not reported; triage service-time field missing in 55.07% of the record set.
quantity: Triage service-time specification used in the DES model
unit: minutes; ARENA LOGN/EXPO parameter units and convention as stated by paper
distribution_family: T1 shifted lognormal; T2 shifted exponential
parameterization: Table 7 reports T1 1.5 + LOGN(1.86, 1.32), but the appendix fit table reports T1 1.5 + LOGN(1.05, 0.848); both report T2 1.5 + EXPO(1.7). Expressions are copied as printed; ARENA parameter convention is not reinterpreted.
fit_method: Appendix reports Kolmogorov-Smirnov and chi-square tests with p<0.05 for both triage shifts; the body states all adhesion-test p-values exceeded 0.05. T1 expression also conflicts between Table 7 and the appendix.
source_evidence_basis: Primary article reports candidate fitted simulation expressions but contains internal contradictions in both T1 parameterization and goodness-of-fit conclusions.
limitations: Triage duration missingness is 55.07%; stage n is not reported. T1 expression and goodness-of-fit conclusions conflict internally, so these figures are not ready for quantitative model use.
inferred_scenario_use: Preserve both reported T1 expressions for traceability, but block quantitative use pending source-resolution; do not assume correlations or RWJ applicability.

source_title: Performance evaluation of an emergency department in Rio de Janeiro: a hybrid approach using Discrete Events Simulation and Data Envelopment Analysis
locator: Results, Table 7 (simulation input); Appendix, distribution-fit table (consultation inputs and fit statistics); statistical data analysis section (claimed goodness-of-fit result).
source_setting: Single emergency department in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil; simulation distinguishes daytime T1 and nighttime T2 physician care.
source_period: Underlying hospital records cover monthly data shown February 2022 through July 2023; exact fitting window not specified.
source_n: Underlying stage sample n not reported; consultation duration field missing in 16.46% of records.
quantity: Emergency consultation service-time specification used in the DES model
unit: minutes; ARENA GAMM/EXPO parameter units and convention as stated by paper
distribution_family: T1 shifted gamma; T2 shifted exponential
parameterization: Table 7 and appendix both report T1 2.5 + GAMM(5.78, 1.29) and T2 4.5 + EXPO(6.49); expressions are copied as printed and source-software parameter convention is not reinterpreted.
fit_method: Appendix reports Kolmogorov-Smirnov and chi-square tests with p<0.05 for both consultation shifts; the body states all adhesion-test p-values exceeded 0.05.
source_evidence_basis: Primary article reports candidate fitted simulation expressions, but its appendix fit diagnostics conflict with the body conclusion that all fit tests had p>0.05.
limitations: Consultation duration missingness is 16.46%; stage sample size is not reported. Contradictory fit-test reporting and unspecified software parameter convention constrain reproducibility.
inferred_scenario_use: Retain expressions as reported, but block quantitative use pending review of the conflicting goodness-of-fit conclusions and parameterization; do not infer dependence or RWJ applicability.

source_title: Discrete-event simulation and design of experiments to study ambulatory patient waiting time in an emergency department
locator: Table 5, statistical distributions of service times used in simulation; Table 1 and study description for sample/setting.
source_setting: Ambulatory emergency patients at a hospital ED in Quebec, Canada; physician/nurse/admin work and patient trajectories modeled.
source_period: One week of patient-flow data collection; exact calendar dates not reported in inspected article.
source_n: 1,035 ED arrivals observed during the collection week; 640 ambulatory patients (395 stretcher patients). Service-time fitting sample counts not given.
quantity: Triage service-time distribution used in the DES model
unit: minutes; parameter convention as printed in source
parameterization: LOGN(5.74, 3.816) min, reproduced as printed; source does not clearly state parameter convention in the table.
source_evidence_basis: The paper calls these statistical distributions used in the simulation; they are model inputs and should not be claimed as verified empirical fits absent a reported fitting procedure.
limitations: Single ED and ambulatory population; fit sample size and fitting method not reported; distribution parameter convention is under-specified. Not an RWJ observation.
inferred_scenario_use: Candidate external distribution for sensitivity only after resolving parameter convention; keep distinct from empirical mean data and do not treat as a local model default.

source_title: Discrete-event simulation and design of experiments to study ambulatory patient waiting time in an emergency department
locator: Table 5, statistical distributions of service times used in simulation.
source_setting: Ambulatory emergency patients at a hospital ED in Quebec, Canada.
source_period: One week of patient-flow data collection; exact calendar dates not reported in inspected article.
source_n: 1,035 ED arrivals observed; 640 ambulatory patients. Registration-duration fitting sample count is not reported.
quantity: Registration service-time distribution used in the DES model
unit: minutes; triangular minimum, mode, maximum as listed by source
source_evidence_basis: Explicitly a distribution used in the simulation. The article does not state that this triangular input was empirically fitted; this record therefore labels it as a model assumption/input.
limitations: Single ED and ambulatory population; source does not report fit method or sample count for registration time. Triangular parameters are not evidence of observed quantiles.
inferred_scenario_use: External model-input comparator for registration duration scenarios only; maintain the source's assumed status and do not present as an empirical distribution or RWJ timing.

quantity: Physician consultation service-time distributions used in DES
unit: minutes; triangular minimum, mode, maximum as listed by source
source_evidence_basis: The paper lists these as simulation service-time distributions but does not report an empirical fit procedure; treat as model inputs/assumptions.
limitations: Single ED; fit counts and method absent. Triangular specification is not an empirical quantile summary and cannot establish the actual distribution.
inferred_scenario_use: Use only as external assumed ranges for initial/follow-up consultation sensitivity scenarios; do not mix with measured means as if equally evidenced and do not transfer to RWJ.

source_title: Improving Emergency Department radiology transportation time: a successful implementation of lean methodology
locator: Methods, study design (period dates); Methods, theoretical model step 2 and sampling (endpoint, inclusion/exclusion); Results, Table 2 (mean, SD and <=10-minute share).
source_setting: Emergency department of American University of Beirut Medical Center, largest tertiary-care center in Lebanon; all ED plain radiographs meeting study sampling criteria.
source_period: Pre-intervention: 2012-10-17 to 2013-04-17; post-intervention: 2013-05-19 to 2013-11-19; one-month washout. Excludes radiographs 00:00-08:00, and cases leaving against medical advice or transferred to another hospital.
source_n: 6,186 radiographs pre-intervention; 4,879 post-intervention, after stated exclusions.
quantity: Cashier order-processed to radiographer study-initiation transportation TAT (pre/post intervention)
unit: minutes from cashier order processing to radiographer study initiation; percent of radiographs with this interval <=10 minutes
source_evidence_basis: Primary retrospective before/after operational cohort reports means, standard deviations, and an empirical threshold share for 11,065 radiographs. Methods define the measured transport TAT as cashier order processing to PACS-recorded radiographer study initiation. The Discussion later calls it an order-processing-to-study-completion step, which conflicts with the explicit Methods definition; this record follows Methods.
limitations: Single center, plain radiography only, nonrandomized intervention with concurrent ED workflow changes; excludes overnight radiographs and AMA/transfer cases. Mean/SD do not define the full empirical distribution. The paper's Discussion uses a conflicting endpoint description; use the Methods endpoint above.
inferred_scenario_use: External reference for cashier-processed order to imaging study initiation elapsed time, preserving the before/after context and exclusions; do not use as RWJ timing or as imaging processing/read duration.
